title: The prisoners whom Jesus sets free
source_text: Εἶτ᾿ ἐπεί φησιν ὁ Κέλσος· πειστέον οὖν ὅτι παραδίδονταί τισιν ἐπιμεληταῖς τοῦδε τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου, λεκτέον πρὸς αὐτὸν ὅτι σπουδαία ψυχὴ καὶ λυθεῖσα ἀπὸ τῶν τῆς κακίας δεσμῶν καὶ ἐν τῷ βίῳ τῶν, ὡς ὠνόμασεν ὁ Ἱερεμίας, δεσμίων „γῆς“ διὰ τὸν εἰπόντα Ἰησοῦν, ὡς πρὸ πολλοῦ χρόνου τῆς ἐπιδημίας αὐτοῦ προεῖπεν ὁ προφήτης Ἡσαΐας· τί δὲ προειπόντα ἢ „τοῖς δεσμίοις ἐξέλθετε καὶ τοῖς ἐν τῷ σκότῳ ἀνακαλυφθῆναι“; καὶ οὗτός γε ὁ Ἰησοῦς. ὡς ὁ αὐτὸς Ἡσαΐας περὶ αὐτοῦ προεῖπε, „καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου ἀνέτειλε φῶς,“ ὡς διὰ τοῦθ᾿ ἡμᾶς λέγειν· „διαῤῥήξωμεν τοὺς δεσμοὺς αὐτῶν καὶ ἀποῤῥίψωμεν ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν τὸν ζυγὸν αὐτῶν.“ εἰ δ᾿ ἐδύνατο ἀκοῦσαι τῆς βαθύτητος τῶν εὐαγγελίων ὁ Κέλσος καὶ οἱ παραπλησίως ἐκείνῳ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν διακείμενοι, οὐκ ἂν ἡμῖν συνεβούλευσεν οἷς ὠνόμασεν ἐπιμεληταῖς τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου πείθεσθαι. γέγραπται δὲ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὅτι „γυνή“ τις „ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελὲς.“ ἥντινα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν καὶ ὁρῶν παρὰ τίνα αἰτίαν συγκύπτει, οὐκ ἐπιτρεπομένη ἀνακύπτειν „εἰς τὸ παντελὲς,“ εἶπε· „ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἐκ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;“ πόσοι δὲ καὶ ἄλλοι νῦν δεδεμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ σατανᾶ συγκύπτουσιν, οὐ δυνάμενοι δι᾿ ἐκεῖνον „ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελὲς,“ θέλοντα ἡμᾶς κάτω βλέπειν; καὶ οὐδείς γε αὐτοὺς ἀνορθοῖ εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐπιδημήσας λόγος, καὶ πρότερον δὲ θεοφορήσας. καὶ ἦλθέ γε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλευθερῶσαι „πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.“ καὶ περὶ ἐκείνου εἰπὼν μετά τινος πρεπούσης αὐτῷ βαθύτητος τό· „νῦν ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου κέκριται.“ οὐ λοιδορούμεθα οὖν τοῖς τῇδε δαί μοσιν ἀλλ᾿ ἐλέγχομεν τὰς ἐπ᾿ ὀλέθρῳ τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐνεργείας αὐτῶν, προφάσει χρησμῶν καὶ θεραπείας σωμάτων καὶ ἄλλων τινῶν χωρίσαι τοῦ θεοῦ βουλομένων τὴν ἐμπεσοῦσαν ψυχὴν εἰς „τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως“· ἥντινα οἱ νοήσαντες ἀναφθέγγονται τό· „ταλαίπωρος ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος. τίς με ῥύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ θανάτου τούτου;“ ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ εἰκῇ παρέχομεν τὸ σῶμα στρεβλοῦν καὶ ἀποτυμπανίζειν· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ παρέχει τούτοις τὸ σῶμα (ὁ) ὑπὲρ τοῦ μὴ τοὺς περιγείους δαίμονας ἀναγορεύεσθαι θεοὺς ἐπιβουλευόμενος ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν σεβόντων αὐτούς. καὶ θεοφιλές γε τὸ διὰ τὴν ἀρετὴν ἀποτυμπανίζεσθαι καὶ δι᾿ εὐσέβειαν στρεβλοῦσθαι καὶ δι᾿ ὁσιότητα ἀποθνῄσκειν εὐλόγως εἶναι νενομίκαμεν. „τίμιος“ γὰρ „ἐνώπιον κυρίου ὁ θάνατος τῶν ὁσίων αὐτοῦ“· ἀγαθὸν δ᾿ εἶναί φαμεν καὶ τὸ μὴ φιλοζωεῖν. κακούργοις δὲ, εὐλόγως ὑπομένουσιν ἃ διὰ λῃστείαν πάσχουσιν, ἐξομοιῶν ἡμᾶς ὁ Κέλσος καὶ μὴ αἰδούμενος τὴν τηλικαύτην πρόθεσιν παραπλησίαν ἀποφαίνει τῇ τῶν λῃστῶν διαθέσει, ἀδελφὸν ἑαυτὸν ἐν τούτοις ποιῶν τῶν „μετὰ ἀνόμων“ λογισαμένων τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ἐφ᾿ οἷς πεπλήρωται ἡ λέγουσα γραφὴ τό· „μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη.“
pass_a_gloss: Then since Celsus says, one must believe they are handed over (παραδίδωμι) to certain overseers (ἐπιμελητής) of this prison (δεσμωτήριον), it must be said to him that a virtuous (σπουδαῖος) soul, loosed (λύω) from the bonds (δεσμός) of wickedness (κακία) even in the life of those whom Jeremiah named prisoners (δέσμιος) of earth, through Jesus who said, as long before his coming (ἐπιδημία) the prophet Isaiah foretold (προλέγω): and what having foretold but 'to the prisoners, come out (ἐξέρχομαι), and to those in the darkness (σκότος), to be uncovered (ἀνακαλύπτω)'? And this indeed is Jesus, as the same Isaiah foretold about him, 'to those sitting in the region and shadow of death (σκιὰ θανάτου) a light (φῶς) has risen (ἀνατέλλω)', so that because of this we say, 'let us break apart (διαρρήγνυμι) their bonds and cast off (ἀπορρίπτω) from us their yoke (ζυγός)'. If Celsus could hear the depth (βαθύτης) of the Gospels, and those disposed like him against us, he would not have counselled (συμβουλεύω) us to obey (πείθομαι) those he named overseers of the prison. It is written in the Gospel that a woman was bent together (συγκύπτω) and unable to straighten up (ἀνακύπτω) completely (εἰς τὸ παντελές); whom Jesus seeing and seeing for what cause she is bent, not permitted (ἐπιτρέπω) to straighten up completely, said: 'and this one, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound (δέω), behold (ἰδού) eighteen years, ought she not to be loosed from this bond on the day of the Sabbath?' How many others now, bound by Satan, are bent, unable through him to straighten up completely, he wishing us to look down (κάτω βλέπειν)? And no one sets them upright (ἀνορθόω) except the Word (λόγος) who sojourned (ἐπιδημέω) in Jesus, and who also earlier inspired / was God-bearing (θεοφορέω). And Jesus came to free (ἐλευθερόω) all those oppressed (καταδυναστεύω) by the devil (διάβολος). And having said about him with a depth fitting him: 'now the ruler (ἄρχων) of this world (κόσμος) has been judged (κρίνω)'. We do not therefore revile (λοιδορέομαι) the demons (δαίμων) here, but we refute/expose (ἐλέγχω) their workings (ἐνέργεια) for destruction (ὄλεθρος) of the race (γένος) of men, wishing, on pretext (πρόφασις) of oracles (χρησμός) and healing (θεραπεία) of bodies and certain other things, to separate (χωρίζω) from God the soul having fallen (ἐμπίπτω) into the body of humiliation (ταπείνωσις); which those who understood (νοέω) cry out (ἀναφθέγγομαι): 'wretched (ταλαίπωρος) man I; who will rescue (ῥύομαι) me from the body of this death?' But neither do we at random (εἰκῇ) offer (παρέχω) the body to rack (στρεβλόω) and cudgel to death (ἀποτυμπανίζω); for not at random does he offer the body to these, who, for the sake of the earthly (περίγειος) demons not being proclaimed (ἀναγορεύω) gods, is plotted against (ἐπιβουλεύω) by them and by those revering (σέβω) them. And we have held (νομίζω) reasonably (εὐλόγως) that it is God-pleasing (θεοφιλής) to be cudgelled to death for virtue (ἀρετή), racked for piety (εὐσέβεια), and to die for holiness (ὁσιότης). For precious (τίμιος) before the Lord (κύριος) is the death of his holy ones (ὅσιος); and we say it is good also not to love life (φιλοζωέω). Likening (ἐξομοιόω) us to evildoers (κακοῦργος), who reasonably endure what they suffer for robbery (λῃστεία), and not respecting (αἰδέομαι) so great a purpose (πρόθεσις), Celsus declares it similar to the disposition (διάθεσις) of robbers (λῃστής), making himself in these a brother of those who reckoned (λογίζομαι) Jesus with the lawless (ἄνομος); in whom was fulfilled (πληρόω) the scripture (γραφή) saying: 'he was reckoned with the lawless.'
pass_b_english: Then, since Celsus says, “We must therefore believe that they are handed over to certain keepers of this prison,” we must answer him that a virtuous soul is set free from the bonds of wickedness even while it is still in the life of those whom Jeremiah called “prisoners of the earth” (Lamentations 3:34). It is set free thanks to Jesus, who spoke as the prophet Isaiah foretold long before his coming. And what did Isaiah foretell him as saying, if not, “To the prisoners, Come out, and to those in darkness, Be brought to light” (Isaiah 49:9)? This is indeed Jesus, as the same Isaiah foretold of him: “On those sitting in the region and shadow of death a light has dawned” (Isaiah 9:2; Matthew 4:16). And so, because of this, we say, “Let us burst their bonds and cast their yoke away from us” (Psalm 2:3).

If Celsus, and those who are set against us as he is, could hear the depth of the Gospels, he would not have advised us to obey those he called keepers of the prison. It is written in the Gospel that a certain woman “was bent double and unable to straighten herself fully” (Luke 13:11). When Jesus saw her, and saw why she was bent double, not being allowed to straighten herself “fully”, he said, “And this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for eighteen long years, ought she not to have been loosed from this bond on the Sabbath day?” (Luke 13:16). How many others now, bound by Satan, are bent double, unable because of him to “straighten themselves fully”, since he wants us to look downward? And no one sets them upright except the Word who came to dwell in Jesus, and who also inspired men before that. Jesus came to set free “all who were oppressed by the devil” (Acts 10:38). And of the devil he said, with a depth befitting him, “Now the ruler of this world has been judged” (John 16:11; John 12:31).

We do not, then, revile the demons here on earth; rather, we expose their workings for the destruction of the human race. Under the pretext of oracles, of healing bodies, and of certain other things, they seek to separate from God the soul that has fallen into “the body of humiliation” (Philippians 3:21). Those who have understood the soul so fallen cry aloud, “Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from the body of this death?” (Romans 7:24).

Yet we do not offer our bodies to be racked and beaten to death without reason. For the one who is plotted against by the demons and by those who worship them, because he will not let the earthly demons be proclaimed gods, does not give up his body to these things without reason. And we have rightly held that it is pleasing to God to be beaten to death for virtue, to be racked for piety, and to die for holiness. For “precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy ones” (Psalm 116:15). And we say that it is good, too, not to cling to life.

Celsus likens us to criminals, who deservedly endure what they suffer for robbery; and, showing no reverence for so great a purpose, he declares it to be like the disposition of robbers. In this he makes himself a brother of those who reckoned Jesus “among the lawless”, in whose case the scripture was fulfilled that says, “He was reckoned among the lawless” (Isaiah 53:12; Mark 15:28; Luke 22:37).

choices.choice: The opening sentence is an anacoluthon: σπουδαία ψυχὴ καὶ λυθεῖσα has no finite verb, and the participial clauses about Jesus run on. The English makes λυθεῖσα the main verb (‘is set free’), repeats it as ‘It is set free’ to start a new sentence for διὰ τὸν εἰπόντα Ἰησοῦν, and splits off the Isaiah question; no content added. διά with the accusative is rendered ‘thanks to Jesus’ (because of), not ‘through’. ‘Prisoners of the earth’ (δεσμίων γῆς) is Lamentations 3:34, which Origen ascribes to Jeremiah, as the Septuagint tradition does; καὶ ἐν τῷ βίῳ τῶν ... δεσμίων is rendered ‘even while it is still in the life of those whom Jeremiah called’. Isaiah 49:9 matches the LXX (τοῖς ἐν δεσμοῖς ... ἀνακαλυφθῆναι); here τοῖς δεσμίοις, and the infinitive ἀνακαλυφθῆναι is rendered as a command ‘Be brought to light’. The ‘region and shadow of death’ line is Isaiah 9:2 in English numbering (LXX and Hebrew 9:1), but its wording (καθημένοις ... ἀνέτειλε φῶς) follows Matthew 4:16, so both are cited. Psalm 2:3 has the same number in the LXX; in the psalm the words belong to the rebels against the Lord, and Origen turns them against the demon keepers. Psalm 116:15 = LXX Psalm 115:6 (Origen has ἐνώπιον for LXX ἐναντίον). Luke 13:11: γυνή τις is ‘a certain woman’, with only the verse’s wording inside the quotation marks. Luke 13:16: ἰδού (‘behold’) is carried by ‘eighteen long years’. θεοφορήσας (‘who inspired before that’) has no expressed object; ‘men’ is supplied, referring to the prophets and saints before the Incarnation; the verb could also be taken intransitively. ‘Now the ruler of this world has been judged’ joins John 16:11 (κέκριται) with the ‘now’ of John 12:31; both cited. καὶ περὶ ἐκείνου εἰπών is a participle with no main verb, rendered ‘he said’. ‘Body of humiliation’ (Philippians 3:21) lacks ‘our’ here as in the Greek. ἥντινα (feminine) refers to the soul; ‘the soul so fallen’ makes this explicit. τούτοις in ‘does not give up his body to these things’ may mean the torments or the persecutors; left open. The fulfilment formula and wording (μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη) match Mark 15:28, a verse absent from the oldest manuscripts and from many modern Bibles, and Luke 22:37; the source is Isaiah 53:12. The comparison with robbers answers an earlier remark of Celsus not quoted in this chapter.
'even in this life, the life of those' ('this' added) -> 'even while it is still in the life of those'
διὰ τὸν εἰπόντα Ἰησοῦν (διά + accusative): 'through Jesus' -> 'thanks to Jesus', in its own sentence
'And this is indeed Jesus, of whom ... foretold' -> 'This is indeed Jesus, as the same Isaiah foretold of him' (ὡς)
Luke 13:11: stray quotation marks round 'was' removed; γυνή τις -> 'a certain woman' outside the quotation
Every cited verse checked against LXX/NT wording; LXX Psalm 115:6 -> Psalm 116:15 confirmed
